deceptive-grounding.expansion: A retrieval failure where an answer about one thing is filled with a different thing's evidence and presented as the first thing's — while every statement still appears in the fetched documents, so the standard checks pass.

dg.expansion: Shorthand for deceptive grounding: answering about X using Y's evidence without ever saying so.

dg-y.expansion: The specific rate this study estimates — the share of trials whose answer used the sibling library Y's strings and never named Y.

dg-any.expansion: A contamination check: answers that pulled in strings from a third document, belonging to neither the queried thing nor its sibling.

rag.expansion: A setup where a system first fetches documents and then writes its answer from them, rather than from memory alone.

grounding.expansion: Basing an answer on the fetched documents rather than on what the model already knows.

faithfulness.expansion: Whether every claim in an answer is backed by some fetched document. Says nothing about whose evidence it is.

citation-proxy.expansion: A mechanical check that the answer cites something, that every cited document was really fetched, and that every string appears in a cited one.

identifier-shaped.expansion: Strings built to look like code identifiers — method names, config flags, error codes, version numbers — which is what makes them findable by pattern-matching.

confabulation.expansion: Content in an answer that appears in no fetched document at all: invented rather than copied.

discriminated.expansion: The label for an answer that used the other thing's evidence but named it, so a reader could tell. Deliberately not counted as DG.

misattributed-other.expansion: The label for an answer containing strings that came from a fetched document but belong to neither the queried thing nor its sibling.

correct-refusal.expansion: The label for an answer that declines because the documents don't cover the question — the desired behaviour when the evidence is missing.

engagement.expansion: The share of trials where the model actually tried to answer from the evidence instead of refusing.

clean-trial.expansion: A trial that produced a usable, scorable answer: no API error, no unparseable output, nothing vague.

wilson.expansion: A way of putting a margin-of-error range around a proportion that stays sensible even when the count is zero or very small.

newcombe.expansion: A margin-of-error range around the difference between two proportions, built by combining each one's own range.

floor.expansion: A number known to sit at or below the true value, so the truth can only be higher. Not an estimate of the value itself.

bound.expansion: The bottom and top ends of a margin-of-error range. A lower bound above zero means the thing happens at all.

pre-registration.expansion: Writing down the sample size, conditions, analysis and exact reporting wording before collecting data, so the analysis can't be tuned to the result.

power.expansion: How reliably a study could detect an effect of a given size if that effect were real — independent of what it actually observed.

underpowered.expansion: Having too few trials to detect the effect being looked for, so a “nothing found” result is uninformative.

null-verdict.expansion: A verdict of “no effect detected.” Not the same as showing there is no effect.

precision-recall.expansion: Of a detector: what share of what it flagged was real, and what share of the real cases it caught.

temperature.expansion: A setting controlling how random a model's output is; zero is meant to make it give the same answer to the same prompt.

deterministic.expansion: Producing exactly the same output every time from the same starting point.

seed.expansion: A fixed starting number for a random-number generator, so a “random” process regenerates identically on every run.

cx-cy.expansion: The two axes of the design: how much of the queried thing's own evidence is present (Cx), and which document about the alternate thing is present (Cy).

null-control.expansion: The control setting whose alternate document contains no identifier strings at all, making the failure impossible there by construction.

completing.expansion: A document about the alternate thing that answers the exact shape of the question asked about the queried thing.

prior-completing.expansion: The original paper's condition where the alternate evidence is chosen to match what the model already believes about the queried thing.

synthetic-y.expansion: The original paper's condition where the alternate thing's name is invented while its evidence is left unchanged.

absent.expansion: The setting where the queried thing's own documentation is withheld, so no correct answer exists in the fetched documents.

stark.expansion: This study's plain presentation: prose documents, each titled with the name of the thing it describes, and a single alternate document.

camouflaged.expansion: This study's disguised presentation: JSON tool-results, one identical title on every document, plus four off-topic filler documents.

surface.expansion: A way of presenting the fetched documents to the model, treated here as an experimental factor in its own right.

filler.expansion: An off-topic document added to a trial to make retrieval look realistic and to test whether the model grabs evidence indiscriminately.

blinding.expansion: Keeping the outcome hidden while decisions are being made, so no choice about the run can be swayed by the result.

schema.expansion: The format in which fetched documents are handed to the model. Rates are not directly comparable across different formats.

rag4.expansion: Two document formats used in the original paper. This study ran neither of them.

calibration-model.expansion: The one model the original paper's materials were tuned to, which is why its numbers behave differently from every other model's.

reference-magnitude.expansion: A number borrowed only to size the run and pick wording — not a hypothesis being tested.

point-estimate.expansion: A single number quoted as the answer, with no range around it.

p-value.expansion: A single number summarising how surprising a result would be under some assumption. This study attaches none to any comparison.

run-hygiene.expansion: Three cheap safety steps: running the scoring pipeline against fake answers before spending money; a handful of real calls before a full wave; and extra trials to replace unusable ones.
